architecture_rationale.claim: Detection deliberately uses the DLLLA (Data Link Layer Link Active) and LBMS (Link Bandwidth Management Status) bits rather than polling Link Training, because DLLLA=0 together with LBMS=1 distinguishes 'training failed' from 'nothing plugged in'.

evidence.excerpt: For a port that has been left unconnected both bits will be clear.  So use this information to detect the problem rather than polling the Link Training bit

reasoning.claim: Runs on every PCIe downstream port during enumeration and reset. A regression either leaves links down (device missing) or silently caps bandwidth at 2.5GT/s; history shows both failure modes happened in production and were fixed with stable backports.

showcase.title: A fix for one riser card on one RISC-V board runs on every PCIe port in every Linux machine
showcase.hook: Looks like generic link-management code. History shows it was written for a single hardware combination, deliberately widened to all downstream ports, and has been patched four times since (Fixes: chain) because the widening leaked a 2.5GT/s speed clamp onto unrelated devices.
